symptom: Setting memory.max in a cgroup has no effect; child cgroups can't be created

diagnostic_steps.expected: includes 'memory cpu io pids' for full functionality

fix_steps.validation: child cgroups now have memory.max etc.

fix_steps.action: For systemd-managed, set in unit file

symptom: Cannot move a process into a cgroup that already has child cgroups: EBUSY

diagnostic_steps.expected: presence of subdir = leaf rule violated

fix_steps.action: Move process into a leaf cgroup (create one if needed)

symptom: `unshare -U` or container creation fails 'Permission denied' on Ubuntu 24.04+

diagnostic_steps.action: Check if generic userns sysctl also off

symptom: `ps` inside container shows accumulating <defunct> processes; PID 1 ignores SIGCHLD

diagnostic_steps.expected: shell or app, NOT a real init

diagnostic_steps.command: docker exec <c> ps axo pid,ppid,stat,comm | awk '$3 ~ /^Z/'

fix_steps.action: Run container with init shim (tini, dumb-init, docker --init)
Or, write your app to install SIGCHLD handler / waitpid loop
fix_steps.command: # in app: signal(SIGCHLD, reaper); reaper does while(waitpid(-1,&st,WNOHANG)>0);

symptom: `ls /proc/*/ns/` accumulates after many container creations; eventually 'Too many open files' on namespace FDs

diagnostic_steps.action: Count namespace FDs held by a process
Find process holding lots of /proc/*/ns/* opens
diagnostic_steps.command: sudo lsof | grep '/ns/' | awk '{print $1,$2}' | sort -u | head

fix_steps.action: Close namespace FDs in your code (or upgrade leaking tool)

symptom: Recently-built glibc apps fail inside older container with EPERM; strace shows clone3 → EPERM

diagnostic_steps.command: # inspect runtime: docker inspect / kubectl describe / runc spec

fix_steps.command: # moby seccomp default profile: allow clone3 (added moby v23+); update runtime

fix_steps.action: Workaround: build app against older glibc that uses clone

symptom: Permission denied even with full Linux DAC perms; chmod 777 doesn't help

fix_steps.action: For AppArmor: switch to complain mode for the profile

symptom: Process has cap in PERMITTED but not EFFECTIVE; operation fails

fix_steps.action: Set ambient cap on the process tree
fix_steps.validation: CapAmb shows the cap; child inherits in CapEff

symptom: chroot'd process accesses files outside chroot via existing FD or chdir

diagnostic_steps.command: # chroot does not unmount/move root; FDs opened pre-chroot still resolve

fix_steps.action: Use pivot_root inside a mount namespace (container-style)
fix_steps.command: # unshare -m; mount --bind newroot newroot; pivot_root newroot newroot/.oldroot; umount -l .oldroot

symptom: Reading /proc/self/status from a thread shows main-thread fields, not the thread
Bursty workload throttled even though long-run CPU usage well under quota

fix_steps.action: Increase quota window (longer period accommodates bursts)
fix_steps.command: # echo '500000 1000000' | sudo tee cpu.max  # same 50% but 1s window
fix_steps.validation: nr_throttled stops increasing for same load

symptom: Outbound clients fail EADDRNOTAVAIL after burst of short-lived connections

fix_steps.action: Use connection pooling in the app
fix_steps.command: # keep persistent HTTP/2 / gRPC connections; HTTP keep-alive

symptom: Small TCP requests work; large payloads or HTTPS handshake hang

diagnostic_steps.command: # tcpdump on egress for type 3 code 4 inbound

fix_steps.command: sudo nft add rule ip filter forward tcp flags syn tcp option maxseg size set rt mtu

symptom: After IP move, host can't reach VIP for 5-30s; arp -an shows wrong MAC

fix_steps.action: Send gratuitous ARP from new owner

symptom: Linux router not forwarding packets between interfaces
Asymmetric IPv6 routing drops packets silently
Allow rule placed but traffic still blocked; jump to chain returns earlier

diagnostic_steps.command: sudo iptables -L -nv --line-numbers; sudo nft -a list ruleset

symptom: Reply traffic doesn't get the right fwmark; routing rule mismatches

fix_steps.command: sudo iptables -t mangle -A PREROUTING -j CONNMARK --restore-mark; sudo iptables -t mangle -A OUTPUT -j MARK --set-mark 0x1; sudo iptables -t mangle -A OUTPUT -j CONNMARK --save-mark

symptom: App using EPOLLET stops getting events for some FDs even though data arrived

diagnostic_steps.action: Check if app drains FD until EAGAIN
diagnostic_steps.command: # strace shows partial read then idle; FD never re-armed

fix_steps.action: On EPOLLET, loop read() until EAGAIN before going back to epoll_wait
fix_steps.command: # while ((n = read(fd, buf, sizeof buf)) > 0) {...}; if (errno != EAGAIN) handle

symptom: With SO_REUSEPORT and N workers, one worker gets all connections under low load

fix_steps.command: # attach BPF to choose worker by 4-tuple

fix_steps.action: Or switch to multi-accepter pattern (single listener, N workers accept)

symptom: Server gets wrong UID via SCM_CREDENTIALS on AF_UNIX

fix_steps.action: Enable SO_PASSCRED on receiver before recvmsg

symptom: Idle TCP connections through NAT are silently dropped after ~5 minutes
Modern app fails to init io_uring; falls back to epoll or errors

fix_steps.action: Add io_uring_setup, io_uring_enter, io_uring_register to seccomp allowlist

symptom: Cross-layer rename fails 'invalid argument' or moves whole directory
Deleted-in-upper file still appears in container directory listing
After hard power-off, files written via fsync() lost or corrupted

diagnostic_steps.action: For SAS/SATA SSD, check Power Loss Protection (PLP) capability

fix_steps.action: Disable disk cache (perf cost) for non-PLP devices
Use fsync after every critical write

symptom: `mount --bind -o ro` doesn't actually mark target readonly
Mount inside container leaks to host (or vice versa) unexpectedly

fix_steps.action: Mark mount namespace private at container start

symptom: `/tmp` write fails ENOSPC; size shows 50% but tmpfs default is 50% of RAM
Writes fail / FS goes read-only on thin-provisioned LV; metadata or data pool exhausted

fix_steps.command: sudo lvextend -L+50G vg/thinpool; sudo lvextend --poolmetadatasize +1G vg/thinpool

symptom: `cryptsetup open` fails 'No key available' after re-keying

fix_steps.action: Add new passphrase first, then remove old
fix_steps.command: sudo cryptsetup luksAddKey <dev>; sudo cryptsetup luksRemoveKey <dev>

symptom: Mount slow after crash; dmesg shows 'orphan inode list' replay

fix_steps.command: sudo umount <mount>; sudo e2fsck -y <dev>; sudo mount <mount>

fix_steps.action: Disable lazy itable init or block discard issues

symptom: `umount` fails 'target is busy' even after killing all visible users

fix_steps.validation: detached now; freed when last fd closed

symptom: `/proc/mounts` shows entries no longer mounted; mountpoint missing in `mount`

fix_steps.action: Show namespaced mountinfo (the truth in container land)

symptom: Editor (vscode/jetbrains) fails to watch project: 'too many open files' or watches dropped

diagnostic_steps.expected: default 8192/128 too small for big repos

symptom: `setfattr` fails 'Operation not supported'
App with FAN_CLASS_CONTENT seems hung; access to watched files freezes

diagnostic_steps.action: App must respond to FAN_OPEN_PERM events with FAN_ALLOW/FAN_DENY

fix_steps.action: Always reply with FAN_RESPONSE structure within timeout
fix_steps.command: # write back fanotify_response { fd, response = FAN_ALLOW }

symptom: systemd unit goes 'failed' after StartLimitBurst (5 by default) restarts

fix_steps.command: sudo systemctl reset-failed myapp; sudo systemctl start myapp

symptom: Long-running systemd service killed before finishing graceful shutdown
systemd `<mount>.mount` unit failed; fstab entry has typo or invalid options

fix_steps.command: # correct line; sudo systemctl daemon-reload; sudo systemctl restart <mount>.mount

symptom: `systemctl set-property MemoryMax=2G` does nothing visible; cgroup memory.max unchanged

fix_steps.command: sudo systemctl set-property myapp.service MemoryMax=2G; sudo systemctl daemon-reload

symptom: `systemctl is-active multi-user.target` = active, but app's own service shows 'not yet started'

fix_steps.action: Add WantedBy or Required for boot

symptom: systemd socket unit listening but service isn't started on connect

diagnostic_steps.command: systemd-socket-activate -l 8080 echo hi   # OR  curl localhost:<port>

fix_steps.action: Ensure service file matches socket name
fix_steps.command: # myapp.service paired with myapp.socket; or set Service=myother.service

fix_steps.action: Service must accept fd from systemd
fix_steps.command: # in service: read $LISTEN_FDS, listen on fd 3

symptom: systemd .timer skipped firings; OnCalendar=daily missed days

fix_steps.action: Enable Persistent=true to catch missed runs

symptom: DNS through systemd-resolved stub (127.0.0.53) loops back

diagnostic_steps.action: Confirm /etc/resolv.conf is the symlink to stub

symptom: User code can't write to its own cgroup tree even though it owns the slice
`perf record` fails 'Permission denied' or 'No permission'
Flame graph shows shallow stacks; symbols mostly '[unknown]'

diagnostic_steps.action: Check perf was given DWARF call-graph
diagnostic_steps.expected: yes; fp-only fails for fp-omitted binaries

symptom: `bpftrace` or `bcc` script fails: 'verifier failed' on attach

fix_steps.action: Bound the program: hard-code loop limit, narrow types

symptom: `bpftrace -e 'kprobe:func {...}'` fails 'function not found' but symbol in /proc/kallsyms

diagnostic_steps.action: Inspect /proc/kallsyms (function may be inlined → no kprobe attach point)
diagnostic_steps.expected: present but kprobe still fails = inlined

fix_steps.action: Use kfunc on kernels with BTF (5.5+)

symptom: App becomes 100x slower under `strace -f`; production user-impacting
`gdb -p <pid>` fails 'ptrace: Operation not permitted'
function tracer drops events; trace_pipe shows missed entries
After kernel panic, no /var/crash/* dump produced
`df` shows disk full but `du` adds up to less; `lsof | grep deleted` shows large files

fix_steps.command: sudo systemctl restart <unit>   # OR kill PID

symptom: Disk slow; `iostat -x` shows high await/svctm

fix_steps.command: echo none | sudo tee /sys/block/sdX/queue/scheduler   # for NVMe

symptom: `auditd` floods log; disk fills
`journalctl` shows 'No journal files were found' or 'corrupt'

fix_steps.command: sudo systemctl stop systemd-journald; sudo mv /var/log/journal/<machine>/<file> /tmp/; sudo systemctl start systemd-journald; sudo journalctl --vacuum-size=200M
